answer: The tundra multiplier is published, charged in walnut, and beacon lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 10 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 4889 identities would post 1719 proofs and burn roughly 63 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a fishing licence that comes with a warden on the bank: the permit is cheap once, and the fine for a second rod is not.
